definition: The nucleus of the solitary tract is a region of gray matter in the dorsomedial medulla oblongata that is linked with the solitary tract. It receives input from many body systems, including facial, glossopharyngeal, and vagus nerve endings, and helps coordinate autonomic control of functions such as cardiovascular, breathing, taste, gastrointestinal, and chemical-sensing aspects of homeostasis.
